subject: Cognitive Science
title: Embodied Concepts
description: Learn Embodied Concepts in one minute.

hook.text: Reading the word "kick" activates the same brain area you use to actually move your foot.

buildup.text: Embodied cognition says concepts are grounded in sensory and motor experience, not abstract symbols.

discovery.text: Holding a warm cup makes people rate strangers as warmer. Physical warmth primes social warmth.

twist.text: But patients with motor paralysis still understand action words. Grounding isn't the whole story.

climax.text: Concepts may be hybrid—partly sensorimotor, partly abstract—blending body and language.

punchline.text: Your body is part of how you think.

quiz.question: What does embodied cognition claim about concepts?
options: They are grounded in sensory and motor experience
They exist only as abstract symbols
They are independent of the body
